periods.name: Emergence in Africa
periods.description: The oldest fossils attributed to Homo sapiens, from Jebel Irhoud in Morocco, date to roughly 300,000 years ago. Early sapiens remains are spread across Africa.

periods.name: Early dispersals
periods.description: Fossils in the Levant show that Homo sapiens left Africa at least intermittently long before the main dispersal. How lasting these early groups were is debated.

periods.name: Main out-of-Africa dispersal
periods.description: Genetic evidence indicates that most present-day non-African populations descend from a dispersal roughly 50,000–70,000 years ago.

periods.name: Late Pleistocene
periods.description: Homo sapiens is present across Africa, Eurasia and Sahul. The Last Glacial Maximum peaks around 26,000–19,000 years ago.

periods.name: Holocene
periods.description: The current geological epoch, beginning at the end of the last glacial period. Farming emerges independently in several regions.

sites.name: Jebel Irhoud
sites.description: Fossils dated ~315,000 years ago (±34,000), currently the earliest attributed to Homo sapiens.

sites.name: Omo Kibish
sites.description: Omo I. Age estimates range from ~195,000 to a minimum of ~233,000 years depending on the study.

sites.name: Misliya Cave
sites.description: A modern-human maxilla dated ~177,000–194,000 years ago, among the earliest sapiens evidence outside Africa.

sites.name: Herto
sites.description: Crania from the Middle Awash dated ~154,000–160,000 years ago.

sites.name: Skhul
sites.description: Burials of early Homo sapiens at Mount Carmel, dated roughly 100,000–135,000 years ago.

sites.name: Qafzeh
sites.description: Early Homo sapiens burials near Nazareth, dated roughly 90,000–120,000 years ago.

sites.name: Jwalapuram
sites.description: Stone tools from before and after the ~74,000-year-old Toba eruption; whether their makers were Homo sapiens is debated.

sites.name: Tam Pa Ling
sites.description: Modern human skull dated to at least ~46,000 years ago.

sites.name: Grotte Mandrin
sites.description: Modern-human tooth and tools dated ~54,000 years ago; interpretation debated.

sites.name: Madjedbebe
sites.description: Occupation dated ~65,000 years ago by some, ~50,000 or less by others.

sites.name: Bacho Kiro
sites.description: Among the earliest Homo sapiens in Europe, ~46,000–44,000 years ago.

sites.name: Ortvale Klde
sites.description: Rockshelter recording Upper Palaeolithic occupation from ~42,000–38,000 years ago (approximate location).

sites.name: Lake Mungo
sites.description: Burials showing people in the Australian interior by ~42,000 years ago.

sites.name: Yana RHS
sites.description: Arctic Siberian site occupied ~32,000 years ago.

sites.name: White Sands
sites.description: Human footprints dated ~23,000–21,000 years ago; dating debated.
